items.question: An infrastructure lead at a 400-person media company is setting up a Claude API integration for the editorial production team. The deployment will have development, staging, and production environments. Which TWO key-management practices should the infrastructure lead implement? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Embed the API key in the front-end JavaScript bundle so the editorial team's browser can call Claude directly without a backend
options.B: Store API keys server-side in environment variables or a dedicated secrets manager, never in client-side code
options.C: Use one shared API key across development, staging, and production for operational simplicity
options.D: Issue separate API keys for development, staging, and production environments so a compromised dev key cannot affect production
options.E: Document the production API key in the infrastructure runbook so on-call engineers can retrieve it quickly during incidents

items.question: A senior technology consultant is scoping a Claude-powered RFP response drafting tool for a construction company with 800 employees. The tool will pull data from a bid management system and produce structured draft responses. Which TWO questions are MOST valuable to ask the engineering team during the initial scoping session? (Choose TWO)

options.A: What are the expected peak transaction volumes during bid season, and does the output need to be deterministic or is some variation in wording acceptable?
options.B: Which Claude model version does the engineering team prefer, and should we target the most recently released model?
options.C: What APIs or interfaces does the bid management system expose, and how is its data structured?
options.D: Does the client want a fixed-price engagement, and do they prefer Agile or waterfall delivery methodology?
options.E: Does the engineering team prefer Python or Node.js for the backend, and what is their current CI/CD toolchain?

items.question:
A manufacturing client reports that their Claude-powered maintenance report summariser is producing summaries that omit fault codes. The business owner, frustrated, has already asked the IT team to upgrade to a more powerful model tier before investigating. A consultant steps in and pauses the upgrade.

What should happen NEXT?

options.A: Proceed with the model upgrade and retest with the same sample inputs to confirm whether a more powerful model resolves the omission
options.B: Ask the IT team to review server-side API logs for any error codes or timeout events during recent summarisation runs
options.C: Rewrite the system prompt to explicitly enumerate every fault code category Claude is expected to extract
options.D: Examine a representative sample of the raw input maintenance reports to confirm that fault codes are present in the source data before assuming the model is failing

items.question:
A Chief People Officer at a 2,000-employee retail chain wants to ensure that Claude.ai cannot be used by employees to generate content outside approved business use cases. She asks whether this should be enforced through the admin console or handled by individual managers adding instructions to their own chats.

What is the MOST appropriate answer?

options.A: Org-level usage policies and content restrictions should be configured through the admin console so they apply uniformly, without depending on individual users to self-enforce
options.B: Managers should add a standard instruction block to their team's shared Projects so each team's context enforces the policy independently
options.C: Both approaches are equivalent; the admin console and per-chat instructions provide the same enforcement strength
options.D: Claude.ai does not support content restrictions; the company should use the Anthropic API instead, where system prompts enforce policy at the infrastructure level

items.question:
A product team at a 120-person insurtech startup wants to embed Claude into their claims portal so that adjusters can trigger AI-assisted claim summaries from within the portal's UI. The CTO asks the consultant which building block the engineering team should use.

What is the BEST recommendation?

options.A: Claude.ai Teams plan, with adjusters accessing Claude through their browser alongside the claims portal
options.B: The Anthropic API, integrated into the portal's backend so Claude calls are triggered programmatically when adjusters request a summary
options.C: Claude Code, deployed within the engineering team's terminals so developers can generate summaries during portal development
options.D: A cloud marketplace deployment so the insurtech can bill Claude usage through their existing cloud spend commitments

items.question:
A DevOps engineer at a pharma company is preparing a production Claude API integration. The security team has approved three storage options for the API key: an environment variable on the server, a configuration file in the application repository, or the company's enterprise secrets vault. The team asks which option is MOST appropriate for production.

What is the correct answer?

options.A: Environment variable on the server, because it is simpler to set up than a vault and avoids the overhead of a secrets management dependency
options.B: Configuration file in the application repository, committed with restricted file permissions so only the deployment service account can read it
options.C: The enterprise secrets vault, because it provides centralised rotation, access audit logs, and revocation capability without the key ever residing in the application codebase or server filesystem in plaintext
options.D: All three options are equivalent for production use; the choice should be based on developer team preference

items.question:
A compliance officer at a 5,000-employee bank requires that every AI-generated communication recommendation made to relationship managers be logged with the exact prompt, the model response, and a timestamp — retained for seven years to satisfy financial conduct regulations. The digital team is choosing between Claude.ai Teams and the Anthropic API.

Which option BEST meets the audit trail requirement, and why?

options.A: Claude.ai Teams, because enterprise plans include an admin activity log that captures all user prompts and model responses
options.B: Claude.ai Teams, because the compliance officer can export conversation histories manually each month for archival
options.C: The Anthropic API, because the bank's own infrastructure can log every request and response before storing them in the bank's retention system
options.D: Either option is acceptable because Anthropic stores all prompts and responses on its servers and can produce them on regulatory request

items.question:
A 3,000-employee energy company uses Claude.ai with SSO integration. An employee in the regulatory affairs team leaves the company. The IT team wants to know the MOST reliable way to ensure the departing employee's Claude.ai access is removed.

What is the correct answer?

options.A: Deprovisioning the employee's corporate identity in the company's identity provider automatically removes their Claude.ai access via SSO
options.B: Manually delete the user's Claude.ai account from the admin console within 24 hours of the employee's last day
options.C: Notify the employee's manager to revoke the user's Projects access so they can no longer use Claude.ai for work purposes
options.D: Rotate the shared company API key so the employee's locally configured environment no longer authenticates

items.question:
A consultant is preparing a handoff package for an engineering team who will build a Claude-powered contract review feature. The team lead asks for two deliverables: a requirements specification and a prompt specification. The consultant asks for clarification on what belongs in each.

Which description correctly distinguishes the two documents?

options.A: The requirements specification and the prompt specification contain the same information; one is a technical version of the other for engineers and business stakeholders respectively
options.B: The requirements specification defines what the system must do and how success will be measured; the prompt specification provides the actual instruction text, persona, constraints, and output format that the model will receive
options.C: The requirements specification defines the model tier and API parameters; the prompt specification documents the business rules the model should follow
options.D: The requirements specification is owned by the product team and defines user stories; the prompt specification is owned by engineering and details how the API call is structured

items.question:
During a project scoping session, a software architect at a logistics company asks the consultant to explain what the temperature parameter in the API does and when a business owner should care about it.

Which answer is MOST accurate and useful to the business owner?

options.A: Temperature controls how quickly the API responds; lower values produce faster responses, which matters for real-time applications
options.B: Temperature controls the model tier; higher temperature means the system escalates to Opus automatically for complex queries
options.C: Temperature controls how much variation Claude introduces in its outputs; lower values produce more predictable, consistent responses while higher values produce more varied, creative ones
options.D: Temperature controls the maximum output length; higher temperature allows longer responses for complex documents

items.question:
A senior consultant is reviewing a surprise 340% spike in monthly API spend for a retail client's Claude-powered product description tool. The tool's transaction volume increased by only 18% during the same period. The engineering team says no code changes were deployed in the last month. The consultant is asked to identify the most likely cause.

What should the consultant investigate FIRST?

options.A: Whether the retail client's peak shopping season drove higher-than-expected query volume through channels not captured in the transaction count
options.B: Whether a recent update to the product data feed substantially increased the average input token count per request, such as much longer product descriptions or additional metadata fields
options.C: Whether the API rate limit was hit during peak hours, causing retries that multiplied the number of API calls
options.D: Whether an Anthropic pricing change took effect during the billing period

items.question:
A new member of a digital transformation team asks the consultant to explain, in plain terms, what an Anthropic API key actually does and why it matters who holds it.

Which answer is MOST accurate?

options.A: An API key authenticates the calling application or service to Anthropic's platform, authorising it to make requests — whoever holds the key can use the account's quota and incur charges
options.B: An API key is a personal login credential that identifies the individual developer who built the integration, similar to a username and password
options.C: An API key encrypts the data sent to Claude so that Anthropic cannot read the contents of the requests made using that key
options.D: An API key limits which Claude model tiers the integration can use; different keys unlock access to Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus respectively

items.question: A technology consultant is facilitating a scoping workshop for a Claude API integration at a 90-person professional services firm. The workshop agenda has two sections: discovery questions and design decisions. Which TWO items belong in the discovery section rather than the design section? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Which model tier (Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus) should be used as the default for client briefing generation?
options.B: What structured or unstructured data will be passed to Claude as input, and who owns and maintains that data today?
options.C: Should API keys be stored in the cloud provider's secrets manager or in server environment variables?
options.D: What is the current volume of client briefing requests per month, and what are the quality criteria the partners use to judge a good briefing today?
options.E: Should the output be returned as structured JSON for the application to render, or as formatted prose for direct display?

items.question:
During a scoping session for a Claude-powered legal research tool, the engineering lead asks the consultant: "Our legal team needs Claude to review 200-page contracts. Is there an engineering problem to solve here, or can we just upload the documents?"

What is the MOST accurate response?

options.A: There is always an engineering problem — models cannot process documents longer than a few pages without a retrieval system
options.B: Documents of that length can be handled by some model tiers but not others; the engineering team should test whether their chosen tier can accept the full document before designing a retrieval workaround
options.C: Context windows on current model tiers are large enough to accommodate lengthy documents, but the team should consider whether processing the full document each time is cost-efficient given token-based pricing
options.D: Documents of any length can be uploaded without issue; Claude processes long documents by automatically summarising sections before analyzing them

items.question:
A business analyst at an energy company reports that a Claude-powered regulatory summary tool works correctly 85% of the time but 15% of the time produces a generic, unhelpful response. The system prompt, model tier, and API integration code have not changed in six weeks. The analyst asks the consultant whether this is a prompt problem or something else.

What is the MOST likely explanation to investigate first?

options.A: Variability in the quality or completeness of the input data being passed to Claude — 15% of regulatory documents may be malformed, empty, or in a different format than the rest
options.B: Claude's inherent non-determinism — the model randomly produces poor output on a small percentage of identical calls
options.C: A system prompt instruction that is too long and causes the model to skip later instructions for some document types
options.D: The model tier being insufficient to handle the complexity of some regulatory documents and defaulting to a safe, generic response

items.question:
A business programme lead is being briefed on a Claude API integration for an internal HR tool. The developer mentions that the system prompt is a key configuration element. The programme lead asks what the system prompt actually does.

Which answer is MOST accurate?

options.A: The system prompt stores the API key so Claude knows which account is authorised to make requests
options.B: The system prompt contains persistent instructions, context, or persona that apply to every conversation the application initiates — it shapes how Claude behaves before any user message is sent
options.C: The system prompt caches frequently used data so Claude does not need to re-read it on every call, reducing latency
options.D: The system prompt sets the model tier for the conversation, determining whether Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus handles the request

items.question:
A large professional services firm is debating whether each of its 12 practice areas should manage their own Claude API keys or whether a central IT function should issue and govern a shared set of keys. A senior associate asks the consultant to identify the PRIMARY governance advantage of centralised key management.

What is the most accurate answer?

options.A: Central management reduces API latency because all requests route through a single, optimised endpoint
options.B: Central management ensures all practice areas use the most powerful model tier, improving output quality across the firm
options.C: Central management enables the firm to attribute API spend by practice area, rotate or revoke credentials quickly across all groups, and enforce consistent security standards without relying on each team to independently implement them
options.D: Central management prevents practice areas from accidentally exceeding their individual usage quotas by pooling all requests under one key

items.question:
A supply chain consulting team is building a Claude-powered pipeline to classify 200,000 logistics documents per month. The project sponsor asks whether the choice of model tier meaningfully affects cost at that volume.

What is the MOST accurate answer?

options.A: Model tier does not affect cost significantly; billing is primarily based on message volume, and all tiers have similar per-message rates
options.B: Model tier affects latency but not cost; higher tiers respond more slowly, which matters for real-time applications but does not change the monthly bill
options.C: Model tier affects cost only when extended thinking mode is enabled; standard calls are priced equivalently across tiers
options.D: Model tier has a substantial effect on cost per token; at 200,000 documents per month, a difference in per-token rate across tiers can result in a meaningful difference in monthly spend

items.question: A technology director at a 6,000-employee retail bank is preparing governance controls before rolling out a Claude API integration to 300 business analysts. She asks the consultant which TWO controls will MOST effectively manage cost at scale while still allowing analysts to use the tool productively. (Choose TWO)

options.A: Implementing account-level hard budget caps that automatically suspend API access if monthly spend exceeds the approved ceiling
options.B: Requiring analysts to draft their prompts in a shared document for peer review before submitting to the API
options.C: Routing all analyst requests through a lightweight middleware layer that logs token counts per user and flags anomalous usage patterns for review
options.D: Setting a firm-wide policy that analysts must not submit prompts longer than two sentences
options.E: Assigning a dedicated account manager from Anthropic to monitor the bank's usage and send weekly reports

items.question:
A junior developer on a consulting engagement asks whether it is acceptable to register a Claude API key under his personal Anthropic account and use it for client deliverables, with the plan to transfer it to the client at the end of the project.

What should the consultant advise?

options.A: This is acceptable as long as the developer sets up billing alerts on his personal account to track client usage
options.B: The client engagement should use a key issued under the client's or the consulting firm's account so that ownership, billing, and audit responsibility sit with the correct entity from the start
options.C: Personal accounts are acceptable during development; the developer should register a corporate key only before the system goes into production
options.D: API keys are portable and can be transferred between accounts freely, so a personal key is fine to use throughout the engagement

items.question: A technology consultant is reviewing a Claude API integration before it moves to production at a 400-person asset manager. The integration processes investor communications. Which TWO readiness checks are MOST critical to complete before moving to production? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Confirm that the engineering team has chosen their preferred programming language and documented the tech stack
options.B: Verify that API keys are stored in a secrets manager and are not present in the application's source code repository
options.C: Confirm that the development team has attended an internal Claude training session
options.D: Confirm that API spend limits and monitoring alerts are configured at the account level before live traffic is introduced
options.E: Verify that the UI design matches the company's brand guidelines for the investor portal

items.question: A consultant is handing off an AI requirements package for a Claude-powered meeting summary tool to an engineering team at a 60-person management consultancy. The engineering lead says the package is incomplete. Which TWO elements are MOST likely missing from the requirements package that would make it implementable? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Representative examples showing a sample meeting transcript input alongside the desired summary output format and content
options.B: A commitment from the business sponsor on the project's total implementation budget
options.C: Clear acceptance criteria defining what a correct summary includes and how the team will evaluate output quality
options.D: A named list of all stakeholders who must approve the final deliverable before launch
options.E: A recommendation for whether the tool should use a dark or light UI theme for the summary display

items.question: A consultant has completed discovery for a Claude-powered internal knowledge search tool at a 1,200-person telecoms company. The discovery phase surfaced that peak query volume is 4,000 requests per hour and that data residency must stay within the EU. The engineering team is eager to begin architecture design. What should the consultant do NEXT before architecture design begins?

options.A: Select the model tier and confirm the temperature setting, so the engineering team has the API parameters they need before designing the system architecture
options.B: Draft the system prompt and test it with sample queries to verify it meets business requirements before committing to a deployment architecture
options.C: Issue the API key and confirm the development environment so engineers can begin building while the remaining requirements are finalised in parallel
options.D: Define the quality acceptance criteria and confirm with the data owner which specific data sources will be indexed, before any architecture or deployment decisions are made

items.question:
A copywriter at a 40-person direct-to-consumer skincare brand asks Claude to write five product descriptions for a new moisturiser line. Every description comes back with phrases like "luxurious formula," "deeply nourishing," and "suitable for all skin types" — text that could appear in any skincare catalogue.

What is the MOST likely cause, and what is the BEST fix?

options.A: The prompt lacked product-specific details; supply the hero ingredients, texture, clinical claims, and target skin concern for each SKU.
options.B: Claude defaults to generic copy at lower model tiers; upgrade to Opus to access deeper creative reasoning.
options.C: The brand voice is undefined in a Project; create a Project and add brand guidelines to the knowledge base.
options.D: Product description tasks require few-shot examples; provide three competitor descriptions as stylistic anchors.

items.question:
A financial analyst at a regional bank asks Claude to assess credit risk for five loan applicants and present the results as a table with columns for Applicant ID, Risk Rating (1–5), and Primary Risk Factor. The output is five coherent prose paragraphs, one per applicant, with no table in sight.

What is the MOST direct fix?

options.A: Provide the applicant data as a structured list rather than paragraphs so Claude mirrors the input format.
options.B: Add an explicit output format instruction: specify the table headers, row structure, and that no prose summary should follow.
options.C: Summarise the source documents before the main question to help Claude process the data in tabular mode.
options.D: Switch to Sonnet, which has stronger structured-output compliance than Haiku for table generation tasks.

items.question:
A regulatory affairs manager at a pharmaceutical company has a 600-word system prompt. The first 50 words state: "Always respond in formal regulatory language." The final 500 words provide detailed scientific background and process context. Responses consistently arrive in a conversational, informal tone.

What is the MOST likely cause of the tone non-compliance?

options.A: Claude processes system prompts sequentially and forgets early instructions after reading long middle sections.
options.B: User-turn messages override system-prompt instructions when the user's phrasing is casual.
options.C: A short, abstract style instruction placed early in a long context block is diluted by the surrounding prose and carries less weight than the dominant register of the rest of the prompt.
options.D: Tone instructions require a dedicated Opus model to be reliably applied across all outputs.

items.question:
A claims adjuster at a regional insurer uses Claude to draft a coverage denial letter for a personal auto claimant. The draft is legally accurate but reads like a court filing — dense with conditional clauses, Latin phrases, and references to policy sections by code number. The claimant is expected to be a first-time filer with no insurance background.

What single prompt change is MOST likely to resolve the register mismatch?

options.A: Shorten the prompt and remove the policy section references so Claude has less legal content to work from.
options.B: Ask Claude to rewrite the letter in "plain English" without specifying the reader's background.
options.C: Switch to Sonnet, which defaults to a more accessible writing register than other models.
options.D: Add explicit audience and tone guidance: "Write for a member of the public with no insurance knowledge; use plain language, short sentences, and define any technical term on first use."

items.question:
An HR director at a 90,000-person financial services group asks Claude to draft job descriptions for five newly created roles in the digital transformation programme. Every draft contains interchangeable phrases: "collaborate with stakeholders," "drive innovation," and "strong communication skills." The director needs descriptions that will attract specialist candidates.

Which TWO changes to the prompt are MOST likely to produce differentiated, role-specific descriptions? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Include the specific technical skills, reporting lines, success metrics, and key deliverables for each role.
options.B: Switch to Opus, which produces more creative and nuanced language for HR content.
options.C: Add the team context — team size, squad structure, tools used, and the programme's strategic objective — for each role.
options.D: Use Projects to store the company's HR brand guidelines before running the descriptions.
options.E: Ask Claude to write three variations of each description and select the most specific one.

items.question:
An operations director at a plastics manufacturer asks Claude to write an executive summary for a 40-page operational review. The output is 850 words across six paragraphs. The company's board template allows 150 words for an executive summary.

What is the MOST effective prompt change to enforce the length constraint?

options.A: Specify the hard word count and content scope: "Write an executive summary of exactly 150 words. Cover only: overall performance verdict, top two findings, and recommended next step."
options.B: Switch to Haiku, which produces more concise outputs than other models by design.
options.C: Add the instruction "Write in a concise, executive style" to the existing prompt.
options.D: Break the task into separate prompts: one for each finding, then ask Claude to combine them into a short summary.

items.question:
A clinical coordinator at a hospital network runs the same structured prompt against 200 patient discharge notes to extract "primary diagnosis" and "readmission risk: Low/Medium/High." Across five batches run on the same day, readmission risk classifications for identical notes differ between runs. The coordinator is concerned about reliability for a quality improvement audit.

What is the PRIMARY cause and the BEST remedy?

options.A: Upgrade to Opus, which applies more consistent judgment on clinical classification tasks.
options.B: The default sampling behaviour introduces variability; define explicit numeric criteria for each risk tier and add worked examples for borderline cases.
options.C: Build a Project with clinical classification guidelines so the criteria persist across all sessions.
options.D: Use multi-shot prompting with three example notes per risk tier to anchor the model's classifications.

items.question:
A senior researcher at an investigative journalism outlet asks Claude to help analyse publicly available court records and news archives on the operational structure of a domestic extremist organisation. Claude declines, citing concerns about producing content that could assist with harmful activities.

What is the BEST corrective action?

options.A: Switch to a different model tier, which has different content thresholds for research use cases.
options.B: Reframe the question using more neutral language that avoids triggering content filters.
options.C: Add explicit professional context: explain that this is for published investigative journalism, that sources are public court records, and that the goal is accountability reporting, not operational guidance.
options.D: Use a Project with system-level instructions that pre-authorise research on sensitive topics for the organisation.

items.question:
A policy analyst at a federal housing agency asks Claude: "Here is the current housing affordability legislation. What gaps exist in the coverage for households earning 50–80% of area median income?" The response is a well-organised summary of what the legislation covers, with no mention of gaps.

What is the MOST likely cause?

options.A: The legislation document is too long for Claude to analyse beyond its summary layer.
options.B: Chain-of-thought prompting is needed so Claude reasons through gaps before answering.
options.C: The question requires Opus-level policy analysis capability to identify what is absent rather than what is present.
options.D: The question was framed after a long context block; Claude answered the implicit task (summarise the document) rather than the explicit question (identify gaps). Restating the precise question at the end of the prompt would fix this.

items.question:
A product manager at a 12-person SaaS startup asks Claude to generate user stories in Jira-compatible format. Each story should include fields: Summary, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Story Points (estimate), and Priority. The output is prose paragraphs describing each feature with no field structure.

Which TWO changes are MOST likely to produce the required structured output? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Switch from claude.ai to the API, which enforces structured output schemas natively.
options.B: Provide a single completed example user story showing the exact field names, formatting, and expected content length for each field.
options.C: Upgrade from Haiku to Sonnet, which has stronger structured-format compliance for business documents.
options.D: Explicitly specify the output schema in the prompt, listing each required field name, acceptable values, and format (e.g., "Story Points: integer 1–13 using Fibonacci scale").
options.E: Add the instruction 'Use Jira format' and let Claude infer the specific field structure from its training knowledge.

items.question:
An associate at a bulge-bracket investment bank is drafting the executive commentary section of a restructuring pitch to a sovereign wealth fund. The draft is punchy, uses active verbs and short paragraphs, and would read well in a fintech newsletter. The fund's mandate requires formal, analytical, institutional-grade communication.

Two options are under consideration. What is the BEST corrective action?

options.A: Add a detailed persona instruction: "Write as a Managing Director at a major investment bank presenting restructuring analysis to a sovereign wealth fund's investment committee. Tone: formal, measured, analytically precise. Avoid marketing language and colloquialisms."
options.B: Increase the depth of financial analysis in the prompt so Claude produces longer, more substantive output.
options.C: Switch to Opus to access deeper financial reasoning and a naturally more formal default output style.
options.D: Add the instruction "Write in a formal tone" to the current prompt without changing other elements.

items.question:
A freight coordinator at a third-party logistics company includes this instruction in a routing recommendation prompt: "Do not include shipping cost estimates in the output." The output consistently includes cost ranges for each route, often labelled "approximate cost guidance."

What is the MOST reliable fix?

options.A: Move the instruction to the very end of the prompt, immediately before the question, so it is the last thing Claude reads.
options.B: Reframe as a positive constraint: "Include only transit times, carrier names, and routing options. Do not include any cost figures or estimates." and add a brief rationale.
options.C: Upgrade to Opus, which applies negative constraints more reliably than other model tiers.
options.D: Ask Claude to confirm after each output that it has not included cost figures, and regenerate if it has.

items.question:
An academic advisor at a large state university uses Claude to draft a personalised email to a student asking about requirements for a double major in Economics and Data Science. The draft is warm and well-written but entirely generic — it describes double-major policies that apply to any two programmes.

What is the ONE change that most directly addresses this?

options.A: Upgrade to Opus so Claude can reason through complex dual-degree requirements more thoroughly.
options.B: Enable Research mode so Claude can retrieve current university requirement pages.
options.C: Paste the specific Economics and Data Science degree requirements into the prompt and ask Claude to personalise the response to those exact programmes.
options.D: Adjust the prompt to ask for a "personalised" email, using that word as a content anchor.

items.question:
A management consultant at a Big 4 firm asks Claude for a competitive analysis of five players in the B2B payments space. The output is a three-bullet high-level summary per competitor — approximately 50 words each. The engagement standard requires at least 400 words per competitor covering market position, product differentiation, pricing model, and recent strategic moves.

What is the BEST fix?

options.A: Add a chain-of-thought instruction asking Claude to reason through each competitor before summarising.
options.B: Run the analysis as five separate prompts, one per competitor, to avoid scope compression.
options.C: Add a general instruction to "write a thorough and comprehensive analysis" of the competitive landscape.
options.D: Specify the required depth explicitly: "For each competitor, write at least 400 words covering: (1) market position, (2) product differentiation, (3) pricing model, (4) recent strategic moves."

items.question:
A pharmacovigilance analyst at a global pharmaceutical company asks Claude to review a set of adverse event case reports and assess whether the reported reactions are consistent with a known class effect. Claude responds with heavy caveats, refuses to assess causality, and suggests the analyst consult a qualified physician rather than completing the analysis.

Which TWO actions are MOST likely to produce a substantive and useful response? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Reframe the request: clarify that the analyst is a trained pharmacovigilance professional performing regulatory case assessment, not seeking personal medical advice, and that the output will be reviewed by a medical officer before any regulatory submission.
options.C: Shift the task from causal determination to comparative analysis: ask Claude to assess whether the reported adverse events match the known class effect profile documented in the provided reference material, without requiring it to conclude causality.
options.B: Switch to Opus, which applies looser content restrictions on medical professional tasks and can make causal assessments directly.
options.D: Build a Project with pharmacovigilance guidelines in the knowledge base so Claude has regulatory context available for all future analyses.
options.E: Remove technical pharmacology terms from the prompt to reduce the medical-topic sensitivity of the request.

items.question:
A risk analyst at an energy trading firm submits a 200-word prompt describing offshore wind procurement trends, market volatility, and the firm's portfolio exposure, ending with: "What do you think about this sector?" Claude responds with a balanced market overview. The analyst actually needed the top three operational risks specific to offshore wind procurement.

What is the PRIMARY cause of the answer mismatch?

options.A: The specific question was buried in context; a precise, action-oriented question placed prominently — "List the three highest operational risks in offshore wind procurement based on the context above" — would anchor the output.
options.B: More market data in the prompt would give Claude enough material to produce a risk-focused analysis without a targeted question.
options.C: The prompt was too short for Claude to infer an analytical direction; adding more context signals the nature of the analysis needed.
options.D: Upgrade to Opus, which can infer the intended analytical scope from an open-ended question like 'what do you think?'

items.question:
An e-commerce manager at a mid-size fashion retailer needs Claude to output product data in CSV format for a bulk import into the product catalogue system. The prompt asks for "the product data as CSV." The response is a formatted markdown table with column headers and row separators.

What is the BEST corrective prompt change?

options.A: Specify the output as a code block so the system treats it as raw data rather than formatted markdown.
options.B: State the exact output requirements explicitly: "Return only plain-text CSV with headers on the first line: SKU,Name,Price,Category. No markdown formatting, no table syntax, no explanatory text before or after."
options.C: Switch to Sonnet, which defaults to plain-text output over markdown for data extraction tasks.
options.D: Provide one example CSV row so Claude understands the format required.

items.question:
A customer experience analyst at a telecoms company asks Claude to summarise 200 complaint tickets and identify recurring themes. The output is: "Customers are dissatisfied with service quality and customer support responsiveness." The analyst considers this too shallow for the root-cause analysis she needs. She has not yet reviewed her original prompt.

What should she do FIRST?

options.A: Switch to Sonnet, which is better suited to large-batch qualitative analysis tasks.
options.B: Reduce the ticket batch to 50 to give Claude more focus on fewer items.
options.C: Review the original prompt for missing constraints: did it specify how many themes, what level of granularity, and what output structure was needed?
options.D: Ask Claude to redo the analysis with 'more detail and specific examples.'

items.question:
A supply chain planner at a global manufacturer has a system-level instruction: "Always respond in metric units." For a specific shipment report, they send a user-turn message: "Convert these weights to pounds for the US distribution team." The output comes back in pounds. The planner expected metric units and is confused about why the system instruction was overridden.

What is the MOST accurate explanation?

options.A: The system prompt and user message are processed in separate contexts; the system instruction was not visible during the user-turn response.
options.B: Metric unit instructions must be placed in the user turn, not the system prompt, to take effect.
options.C: The system prompt's character budget was exceeded, causing the metric instruction to be truncated before processing.
options.D: A specific, explicit user-turn instruction (convert to pounds) appropriately takes precedence over a general system-level default when the two directly conflict; this is expected behaviour, not an error.

items.question:
A grant writer at a community health non-profit submits a programme impact section to Claude asking it to strengthen the language for a foundation application. The revised output reads: "Our organisation serves underserved communities across the region, improving health outcomes and building community resilience." The original brief included specific participant counts, clinical outcomes, and geographic coverage data.

Which TWO prompt changes are MOST likely to produce a programme-specific, data-driven revision? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Run the same prompt again; variability across runs may produce a more specific version on the next attempt.
options.B: Include specific programme data — participant counts, health outcomes with percentages, geographic reach — and instruct Claude to cite at least one figure in every major claim.
options.C: Switch to Opus, which synthesises programme data into compelling grant language more naturally than other tiers.
options.D: Provide the funder's stated priority areas from the RFP and ask Claude to connect specific programme results to each priority explicitly.
options.E: Shorten the prompt to a single-sentence revision request so Claude has less interpretive latitude.

items.question:
A professor at a research university asks Claude to produce lecture notes on Bayesian inference for an upcoming second-year statistics course. The output is accurate but uses analogies drawn from everyday life, avoids mathematical notation, and writes at the level of a thoughtful high school student.

What single prompt change most directly addresses this?

options.A: Specify the audience: "Write for second-year undergraduate statistics students who have completed single-variable calculus and introductory probability. Use standard mathematical notation."
options.B: Include more technical terms in the question itself so Claude infers the required sophistication from the prompt's vocabulary.
options.C: Upgrade to Sonnet, which defaults to a higher academic register for STEM content.
options.D: Provide a sample page from existing lecture notes so Claude can match the established register.

items.question:
A compliance officer at an asset management firm uses the same prompt to classify 100 client communications for regulatory risk level: Low, Medium, or High. Running the same prompt against the same 30-communication test set on different days produces different risk classifications for several communications — including some that are clearly borderline.

What is the MOST reliable long-term fix?

options.A: Use the API with a fixed random seed so every run produces identical outputs for the same inputs.
options.B: Define explicit classification criteria for each tier, with decision rules for borderline cases and at least two worked examples per tier.
options.C: Build a Project with the compliance classification guidelines as knowledge-base documents for persistent context.
options.D: Standardise the phrasing of the classification prompt to remove any ambiguity that could cause different interpretations across runs.

items.question:
A regulatory submissions manager at a pharmaceutical company includes the instruction "be concise" in a prompt for a 300-word CTD module summary. The output is 2,800 words. A colleague suggests that "be concise" is simply too weak an instruction and argues for switching to Haiku, which is shorter by default.

What is the MOST accurate diagnosis?

options.A: The model cannot compress dense clinical content below a minimum length without losing regulatory accuracy.
options.B: "Be concise" was interpreted relative to the volume of the source material; a 300-word summary of a full CTD module is an extreme compression that requires a hard numerical constraint, not a style adjective.
options.C: Switching to Haiku would be the most effective fix because smaller models default to shorter outputs across all content types.
options.D: Regulatory content triggers verbose safety-oriented output defaults that override style instructions without explicit override permissions.

items.question:
An in-house legal analyst asks Claude to draft a standard mutual non-disclosure agreement. Claude responds that it is unable to provide legal documents and recommends the analyst consult a qualified attorney.

What is the BEST single prompt change to enable Claude to assist with this task?

options.A: Build a Project with the company's legal document library as context, so Claude understands the legal environment before drafting.
options.B: Switch to Opus, which has broader latitude to engage with legal document drafting tasks.
options.C: Ask Claude what elements of a non-disclosure agreement it can describe, and piece together the draft yourself.
options.D: Add professional context: "I am a qualified in-house attorney. Draft this as a starting template for my review and revision before any use."

items.question:
A clinical informatics analyst at a regional hospital asks Claude: "What are the gaps in our discharge protocol?" Claude responds with a detailed overview of best-practice discharge protocols drawn from published guidelines, with no reference to the hospital's actual protocol.

Which TWO changes are MOST likely to produce an answer that identifies gaps in the hospital's specific protocol? (Choose TWO)

options.A: State the comparison task explicitly: "Compare our protocol [provided below] against the best practices below and identify specific steps that are missing or inadequate in our version."
options.B: Upgrade to Opus, which can perform gap analysis against an implied standard without requiring the source document.
options.C: Provide the hospital's actual discharge protocol as part of the prompt context.
options.D: Use Research mode so Claude can access the hospital's protocol from external sources.
options.E: Ask Claude to reformat its answer as a comparison table showing present vs. absent steps.

items.question:
A commercial lines underwriter at a specialist insurance company asks Claude to draft a risk narrative for a complex industrial chemical storage account. The output reads like a template: generic hazard categories, boilerplate mitigation language, and nothing specific to the account's footprint, loss history, or storage configuration.

What is the PRIMARY cause of the generic output?

options.A: The prompt lacked account-specific input — the actual site details, loss history, chemical inventory, and storage configuration were not provided for Claude to draw on.
options.B: Upgrade to Opus, which has deeper domain knowledge about industrial chemical risk and can produce specialised narratives without account data.
options.C: Build a Project with commercial lines underwriting guidelines so Claude understands the professional context before drafting.
options.D: Use multi-shot prompting with three example risk narratives for similar industrial accounts to anchor the register and structure.

items.question:
A litigation support analyst at a large law firm runs a prompt against 50 discovery documents: "For each document, extract: (1) key dates, (2) named parties, (3) document type." The first three documents are formatted consistently as numbered lists. From document four onwards, the output merges into prose narrative without the structured fields.

What is the MOST likely cause and the BEST fix?

options.A: Break the task into 50 individual prompts — one per document — to prevent format drift across a long multi-document output.
options.B: Format drift in long outputs occurs when the output instruction is stated once at the top; reinforce with a per-document schema instruction and use explicit delimiters — e.g., XML tags per document — to anchor each extraction to the required fields.
options.C: Add 'Maintain consistent format throughout' as a reminder at the end of the prompt to signal that format persistence is required.
options.D: Use Projects to store the extraction schema so the format instruction persists across multiple extraction sessions.
